question: Does strict DFlash or native MTP change complete-answer correctness versus the same target model without speculation, and what are the measured serving trade-offs?

matched_window.selection: first 32 task IDs per primary dataset in frozen manifest order; identical subset across all routes

repeatability.selection: first 8 task IDs per primary dataset

streaming_latency.capture: first nonempty token event, final content, server token usage, total latency

concurrency.selection: same first 32 task IDs per primary dataset

long_context.kind: explicitly synthetic retrieval probes kept separate from accuracy benchmarks

sampling.claim: finite behavior regression only, not a distribution-equivalence proof

preflight_gates: Verify real GPU, driver, memory, disk and existing runtime without overwriting unrelated services.
Pin serving runtime, target and draft snapshots, tokenizer/chat-template hash, exact command and complete dataset manifest.
Use canonical chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking=false, not a text /no_think instruction; inspect a complete response.
Run at least one code and one math canary through generation and scoring for every primary route before full dispatch.
Use an isolated, non-networked unprivileged code-evaluation container; never execute generated code directly in the privileged VM host.
Confirm isolated Azure readback and deallocate control path before long execution.

evidence.denominators: 164 and 500 independently, per route. Errors, empty answers and truncations are reported, not silently dropped.
evidence.resume: skip only validated completed task IDs for this run and protocol hash; never pick best-of retries
